verdicts.notes: B wins on the visible parts of the criterion — the back chevron is a plain top-left chevron, "SUGGÉRÉ" plus "Suggestions basées sur les mots des titres de programmes, pas une évaluation d'admissibilité" keep suggestions visibly suggestions, "Ta cote : 31,20 · saisie par toi" marks the student's own entry, and "Ne constitue pas un conseil d'orientation personnalisé" holds off ranking — while its first screenful puts the title, the one-line purpose and three large chevron rows in the right order. It loses ground badly on density: ~9.5 viewport heights for one onboarding step, no step indicator, and a skip so far below the fold it is effectively hidden, plus a "SUGGÉRÉ" badge on 100% of cards that therefore distinguishes nothing. A is tighter and instantly legible but prints the one label its task depends on backwards and lets its confirm button sit on top of another control, which is the harder failure to excuse.

verdicts.gapA: In the "Objectifs programme" card, remove has no undo and no consequence copy: each row ends at "× Retirer" and the card stops dead after "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · source" — no "Annuler", no snackbar slot, no "Retiré · Annuler" row. Secondary but nearly as damaging, the mini-chart contradicts its own legend "Barre grise : fourchette publiée · point : ta cote": no grey bar is drawn (22,0–22,5 collapses to a single grey dot, 30,5–31,0 to a faint tick) and the green dot lands at roughly the same ~50% spot on both rows, so the picture carries no honest information about distance to the range.
verdicts.gapB: The whole grid answers none of the criterion: no row carries a status word, a published range, or a source/verification stamp, and there is no remove-with-undo — the "Run" row reads "0.9 miles / 1.2 miles / 1.3 miles / 0 miles / 0.5 miles" where pink means one thing and grey another with no legend, target, or threshold stated anywhere; adding a per-row target range plus a state word ("Au-dessus"-style) and a stamp is what it would take to compete.
violationsA: Touch target: the date filter chips "Toutes / 7 jours / 30 jours / 3 mois" measure ~55 device px (~27 CSS px at 2x) tall — well under 44px.
Touch target: the FR/EN toggle in the header is ~65 device px (~32 CSS px) tall.
Touch target: the "source" links in every stamp ("Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · source", "Vérifié le 24 août 2026 · source" ×16) are bare underlined ~12px text with no padded hit area.
violationsB: Figures with no source and no verification date, and not visibly marked as the student's own entry: "0.9 miles", "1.2 miles", "50 pages", "38 pages", "100 pages".
Dates carry no source or verification stamp and are truncated to weekday+day with no month or year: "THU 29", "WED 28", "TUE 27", "MON 26", "SUN 25".
verdicts.notes: A is the only screen that even attempts the brief — each node shows the range ("Cotes publiées 2024–2025 : 22,0–22,5"), a status word ("Au-dessus"), a stamp, and in-place add/remove — but undo is nowhere on screen and the targets card is a thin slice buried between the hero and a 16-item "Dates importantes" list that swallows roughly 80% of a 7834px scroll, so the screen's own subject is not what you read first. B is cleanly built and legible at arm's length, yet its check/× cells and colour coding have no stated meaning and it offers nothing the criterion asks for. One honesty flag on A worth checking at source: a medicine cutoff of 22,0–22,5 sitting far below architecture's 30,5–31,0 makes the green "Au-dessus" on the most competitive programme the most consequential and least plausible number on the page.

verdicts.gapA: The whole top half is overhead: the app bar already shows "R : 31,20", then a full-width card repeats "Calculé avec ta cote / 31,20", then a search field, then four count cards (two of them dead zeros — "Dans la fourchette 0", "Pas encore vérifié 0"), so "PROGRAMMES TROUVÉS 237" does not appear until roughly halfway down and only two-and-a-bit of 237 rows are visible. Those four count cards are also the tier chips, yet they are drawn as flat white readouts with no pill, border or pressed state — nothing about them says tappable, unlike the university row right below where "Toutes les universités" is an obvious blue pill; collapse the duplicate score card, drop or grey-collapse the zero tiers, and give the tiers the same chip affordance as the university filter.
verdicts.gapB: The floating mini-player is parked over the list and eats the bottom row: "Coffee Run - Blender Open Movie" keeps its title and "Blender Studio" but its view-count/age line is covered, and the player's own label is cut to "Spring - Blender Open Mo.." with "Blender Studio" sitting on a semi-transparent strip where a thumbnail bleeds through behind the text. Separately, this screen offers no counts and no filter row at all — nothing tells you how many results there are or lets you narrow them, so it cannot answer the question the list is supposed to answer.
violationsA: Sub-44px tap targets: the underlined "source" link on each row renders at roughly 12pt tall, and the bell icon in the app bar is a similarly small hit area

Bare figure without label or source: the app bar shows "R : 31,20" with no indication it is the student's own entry and no source or date, and "R" is unexplained jargon (the card below does it correctly with "Calculé avec ta cote")
violationsB: Truncated label: the mini-player reads "Spring - Blender Open Mo.."
Overlapping content: the mini-player overlay sits on top of the "Coffee Run - Blender Open Movie" row, hiding its metadata line, and its text sits over a bleeding-through thumbnail
Figures with no source or verification date: "1.3M views • 5 months ago", "9.1M views • 4 years ago", "4.2M views • 1 year ago" are presented as confirmed with nothing attached
verdicts.notes: A actually does the job under test and its arithmetic is honest — 232 + 0 + 5 + 0 = 237, matching "PROGRAMMES TROUVÉS 237" — and every cutoff carries its provenance ("Cotes publiées 2024–2025 : 22,0–22,5" with "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · source"), with no recommendation or admission-odds copy anywhere. Its craft failure is density and affordance, not truth: half the viewport is spent before the list starts, the tier counts do not look pressable, and the two-dot range track is unlabelled at its ends so the green marker's position is uninterpretable. B is the faster scan of the two, but it is a generic media list with a truncated, content-occluding overlay and no counts or filters at all.

verdicts.gapA: Not one date on the screen is stamped: the header reads "Dec wk. 1" over bare day heads "S 31 / M 1 / T 2 / W 3", with no year, no source and no verification date anywhere, and the only period control is an unlabelled green slider whose value ("7 days") sits at the far right with no indication of what happens at the other end — if every date carried a year plus a source/verified line, this screen would at least be in the argument.
verdicts.gapB: The filter row "Toutes / 7 jours / 30 jours / 3 mois / Cette année" carries no per-chip counts and no disabled or empty-state guard, while the header says "16 dates" and the earliest item is "15 octobre 2026" against a newest stamp of "Vérifié le 24 août 2026" — tapping "7 jours" or "30 jours" empties the whole list with nothing on screen to warn or explain; the same chips are also only ~25 CSS px tall and wrap so that "Cette année" is orphaned alone on a second row.
violationsA: Truncated/broken labels: the 2 PM block reads "Webinar on Lead ership" (word split mid-word across lines) and the bottom category row is cut to "Profe" at the right edge, with its colour strip clipped by the screen edge
Dates carry no source and no verification date and are not visibly marked as the user's own entries — "Dec wk. 1", "S 31", "M 1", "T 2" have no year and no provenance
Sub-44px tap targets: the "Task" chip at 05:00 PM is roughly 16px tall, and the day-column event blocks ("Guitar Practice", "Yoga Session") are ~27px wide
violationsB: Tappable filter chips "Toutes", "7 jours", "30 jours", "3 mois", "Cette année" measure 50px in a 2x 780-wide capture, i.e. ~25 CSS px tall — well under the 44px minimum; the per-entry "source" links are smaller still
verdicts.notes: B is the only one of the two that is actually a dated-deadlines screen: absolute dates throughout (correct, since the nearest is 15 octobre 2026 and nothing is imminent), every entry closed with "Vérifié le 24 août 2026 · source", and a footer that says plainly where figures come from and that "Ta cote R est celle que tu as saisie". Its weaknesses are craft, not honesty — undersized chips, an orphaned "Cette année", 16 near-identical timeline cards with no month grouping or "next up" emphasis, and a legend that promises "Barre grise : fourchette publiée" but draws only two dots on a hairline. A is a store-listing composite ("Your Day, Unfolded", device bezel, ~25% of the frame spent on marketing chrome) whose own content breaks mid-word and clips at the edge, so it loses on the criterion and on craft simultaneously; separately, "Cotes publiées 2024–2025 : 22,0–22,5" for a medicine MD reads as placeholder-grade data even though it is correctly sourced.

verdicts.gapA: The hero card is mistitled against its content: "Cote R d'admission / Automne 2026" leads with "TA POSITION 31,20" in large blue type, while the published cutoff — the one number this screen exists to show — never appears as a figure at all, only as an unlabelled dashed line captioned "seuil 2024–2025" on a bell curve with no axis values. A skimmer reads 31,20 as the admission cutoff. Put the cutoff figure (with its stamp) as the card's hero and demote "ta position" to a comparison line; also label the dashed threshold with its value, and fix the self-contradictory blurb "Formation universitaire de 1er cycle menant au baccalauréat en Doctorat de 1er cycle en médecine (MD)".
verdicts.gapB: Nothing on this screen is a programme detail — it is a channel listing ("Blender Studio", "415K subscribers", VIDEOS/SHORTS/LIVE tabs, a video feed) with no cutoff history, no prerequisites and no add-to-targets control; every figure it does show ("28K views • 1 week ago", "53K views", "9.3K views") is bare of any source or verification stamp. Closing the gap means building the screen the brief asks for, not adjusting this one.
violationsA: Header chip "R : 31,20" (top bar, beside the R logo) shows a figure with no adjacent source, no verification date and no visible marking that it is the student's own entry — the disclaimer that explains it sits in the page footer, far below the fold.

The bell-curve threshold "seuil 2024–2025" is drawn as a dashed line with no value and no axis, so the plotted cutoff is a figure the reader cannot verify against the stamped "Historique des seuils" rows (22,0 / 22,5).
violationsB: "415K subscribers" under the channel name, and "28K views • 1 week ago", "53K views • 1 week ago", "9.3K views • 3 weeks ago" in the feed: every figure sits with no source and no verification date.
Truncated label: the tab strip is clipped at the right edge to "CHAI" (CHANNELS), a cut-off label at the screen boundary.
Video durations "3:33", "21:12", "10:57" are overlaid on thumbnail art ("PRODUCTION LOG 05" runs under the 10:57 chip), producing overlapping text.
verdicts.notes: A is the only screen that attempts the brief and it largely lands it: "Vérifié le 25 août 2026 · source" sits under each number block, the prerequisite badge "DEC REQUIS, AUCUN COURS PRÉCIS" states a catalogue fact rather than advice, and "Ajouté à tes cibles" is well above the fold at full-width tap size. Its real weaknesses are craft, not compliance — a hero number that is the student's own rather than the cutoff, two links labelled only "source" against a third labelled "ulaval.ca", and a dead ~200px band of empty ground between the last card and the footer. B is a different product's channel page and cannot be scored on the criterion at all.

verdicts.gapA: The delete block is not visibly two-step: the card "Supprimer mon compte" / "Supprime définitivement ta cote, tes cibles et tes étiquettes. Cette action est irréversible." ends in a single red link "Supprimer mon compte" with no visible second gate and no copy saying what comes next (no "Tu devras confirmer", no typed-name field, no disabled-until-confirmed state) — a one-tap-looking destructive link is exactly the failure this criterion is meant to catch, and adding a visible confirm step would settle the win condition instead of leaving it to faith.
verdicts.gapB: The screen has none of the criterion's machinery at all: below "Tusky @Tusky@mastodon.social" the only controls are "Unfollow", a bell, a "⋮" menu and a free-text box "Your private note about this account" — there is no edit link that returns to a step, no tag list explaining what a tag unlocks, and no delete-account path anywhere; adding an owner-editable identity section with a guarded delete is the only change that could move the pick.
violationsA: Header pill "R : 31,20" shows a score with no source and no date beside it; the detail row reads "31,20 (confirmée)" with caption "Confirmée par ton cégep · Saisie par toi", which both claims third-party confirmation and self-entry, and carries no verification date

Footer claims "Seuils, dates et bourses viennent de sources publiques, vérifiées à la date indiquée" but no date is indicated anywhere on the screen — a verification claim with nothing to verify against
violationsB: Overlapping/truncated text at the bottom: "Pixelfeds Mastodon Api compatibility" runs under the blue compose FAB, and the "Tusky boosted / Conny Duck" row is clipped at the right edge mid-character
Figures "2,880 Posts", "15 Follows", "21,000 Followers" sit with no source label and no as-of date; "21,000" is a rounded value presented in the same weight as the exact ones, readable as confirmed
verdicts.notes: A actually attempts the brief — two \"Modifier\" entry points, and a tags card that states the payoff ("Sert à faire remonter des bourses auxquelles tu pourrais être admissible") plus what the chip number means — while B is a follower-facing social profile that answers none of it. A's craft is uneven: the chip grid wraps raggedly with dead space to the right of "Engagement communautaire" and "Bénévolat", and "Entrepreneuriat" and "Mobilité internationale" carry no count while every neighbour does, so the reader cannot tell whether that means zero or unknown. B's hierarchy is also wrong for a profile — the loudest element is "Unfollow", and the bio's two-column link table centres wrapped URLs against right-aligned labels.

verdicts.gapA: Hierarchy inside the card: the money is the loudest thing on every row, so you read amounts before you read what the bursary is — "100 000 $ – 120 000 $" is set larger and heavier than its own title, which is squeezed into a half-width column and wraps to five short lines ("Bourse Schulich Leader (STIM / Sciences, Technologie, Ingénierie, Maths)") beside a large empty block under the amount; give the title the full width and demote the amount to a secondary line and the card stops reading like a price list.
verdicts.gapB: The screen never does the job: there are no matched/close/other sections and no why-chips anywhere — the rows are "MORE LIKE THIS", "VIEW MAIN PAGE", "ROLL THE DICE" — and the top third is marketing copy, "Customize the Explore feed to show things that interest you", over a starfield with a device bezel, so roughly half the pixels carry no product content at all.
violationsA: Top bar displays the figure "R : 31,20" with no source, no verification date and no visible marker that it is the student's own entry; the only disclosure, "Ta cote R est celle que tu as saisie", sits in the page footer thousands of pixels below.
The chip "À 0,8 de la cote requise" states a derived numeric gap without showing the cutoff it is measured against and without an ≈ or estimate marking, so it can be read as a confirmed figure.
violationsB: Labels and content are truncated by the frame at both edges: the top row "MORE LIKE THIS" is clipped by the header and the "Echo parakeet" card is sliced mid-content at the bottom of the viewport.
Dated figures "Main page on 25 Jun 2019" and "20 Jun 2019" appear with no source attribution and no verification date beside them.
verdicts.notes: A satisfies the visible criterion outright — three colour-distinguished headings ("Admissible maintenant" green, "À portée" rust, "À explorer" grey), a why-chip on every card ("Ta cote R", "Ton programme", "Ton cégep"), all rows Québec/Cégep de Sainte-Foy with a per-card "Vérifié le 24 août 2026 · source" line, and honest empty states ("Aucune date limite publiée", "Pas de formulaire en ligne. Contacte les services aux étudiants de ton cégep."). Its real weaknesses are craft, not truth: money-first hierarchy, a lot of dead space in the right column, and chips so low-contrast and generic that "Ouvert à tous" is the absence of a match reason rather than one. B is an app-store promo frame of an unrelated feed and cannot compete on the brief at any level.

verdicts.gapA: A is not a notifications screen at all and only half of it is a screen: the top ~380px is store-marketing copy ("Customizable" / "Many customization options, encryption and backups") and a device bezel eats another band, so the actual list ("App" → Theme / Dynamic colors / Language, "Entries" → View mode / Show icons / Code digit grouping) gets under half the frame and is sliced mid-row at the bottom on "Show the account name". Closing it means showing the real screen edge-to-edge; even then, four of the seven rows (Theme "Selected: Light theme", Language "System default", View mode "Selected: Normal", Code digit grouping) carry no chevron, no toggle, no affordance that they open anything.
verdicts.gapB: The guest state is asserted but not actionable: "Enregistré sur cet appareil. Connecte-toi pour retrouver ces choix sur tes autres appareils." sits as low-contrast grey body text below the card, outside any container, with no tappable sign-in control — it names the remedy and then offers no way to do it. Second-order in the same region: all four toggles are identically grey/off with nothing marking that a change was saved, so the "persists offline" promise rests entirely on that one sentence.
violationsA: Truncated label at the frame edge: the bottom row "Show the account name" is cut off mid-row with its subtitle missing
violationsB: Figure without adjacent source/verification: "R : 31,20" in the top bar carries no source or date beside it; the only disclosure ("Ta cote R est celle que tu as saisie") is grey footer text roughly a full screen below it
verdicts.notes: B does the job the brief describes — four rows, each with a plain-language consequence ("Dès qu'un seuil officiel d'admission change pour l'un de tes programmes cibles"), no push block, no recommendation or admission-chance copy — while A is an appearance screen wrapped in store marketing. B's craft is not clean either: a dead ~200px band between the device note and the legal footer, then another gap before the tab bar, so the page ends in wasted space while its most important sentence (the guest note) is the least visible thing on it. The R-score chip is the one honesty problem worth fixing — put the "saisie par toi" mark on the figure, not 1800px away.
